title: Remove inverse K from noncommuting channel comparison by operator covariance
statement: For positive three-output mixtures W_y summing to I, [B^T diag(W_y^-1) B]^-1=diag(W_1,W_2)-w w*. Let D=PKB and H_L=J_L^-1. Then J_K<=c J_L iff D H_L D^T<=c M_K^-1, even when K and D are singular. With x_i=PK[:,i], T_i=diag(x_i)-x_i x_i^T and S_i=D H_i^L D^T, the difference equals sum_i(c T_i-S_i) tensor Q_i+(c-1)V(Q).

body: Use ordered block multiplication, not commutation. Set B=[[1,0],[0,1],[-1,-1]], P=[[1,0,0],[0,1,0]], e1=(1,0),e2=(0,1),e3=0. Form R=P L^-1 with columns r_y, M_i=sum_y L[y,i] r_y r_y^T, H_i^L=M_i-e_i e_i^T, and H_L=sum_i M_i tensor Q_i-q q*, q=(Q1,Q2)^T. Write J_K=D^T M_K D; Z=M_K^(1/2)D J_L^-1/2 gives equivalent Z*Z and ZZ* norm tests without inverse D. Matrix covariance V=sum_i x_i x_i^T tensor Q_i-X X* is positive by an explicit sum of squares. This supplies a quadratic noncommutative positivity problem, including singular K.
